items.title: Canada welcomes EU proposal to become 'associate member'
items.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a Canada-EU alliance would create a "beacon for other democracies".

items.title: Ninth woman's body found as South African police investigate string of deaths
items.description: South Africa police have cautioned against assuming that all the killings are linked but many women are afraid.

items.title: UN experts say grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran strikes
items.description: The US has not acknowledged carrying out February's deadly strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd.

items.title: US to allow Iran delegation to attend UN meetings in New York as war passes half-year mark
items.description: The BBC understands Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi are among the delegates allowed to enter the US.

items.title: Wife of US scholar jailed in China asks Trump to raise arrest at Xi meeting
items.description: Sylvia Zin is among the family members of people imprisoned in China who are seeking Trump's help when he hosts the country's leader next week.

items.title: Hyrox athlete apologises for continuing race after soiling herself
items.description: Joanna Wietrzyk has also forfeited her win in the fitness competition after competing last week.

items.title: Aztec document goes on display in Mexico after 186 years abroad
items.description: France's national library is lending the manuscript recounting the history of the Aztecs to Mexico.

items.title: Assad regime planned US journalist's kidnap for weeks, BBC finds
items.description: Austin Tice’s abduction was approved by Syria’s former leader Bashar al-Assad, a source claims.

items.title: EU announces plan to restrict social media access for under-15s
items.description: Under the plans, only children over 15 would be able to set up their own social media accounts.

items.title: Uncontrolled AI could lead to 'silicon species' rivalling humans, warns Microsoft
items.description: Mustafa Suleyman says he believes rival AI firm Anthropic is in effect teaching Claude it "may be conscious".

items.title: Swedish PM Kristersson resigns after election loss
items.description: Left-wing opposition parties led by Magdalena Andersson look set to form the next government.

items.title: Klopp wants to 'reclaim' flag amid German elections
items.description: New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right election victory.

items.title: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
items.description: Rates were hiked in a unanimous decision despite fierce opposition from President Donald Trump, who had called for a cut.

items.title: Abducted South African journalist found dead with gunshot wounds
items.description: The body of veteran broadcaster Owen Ndlovu was found hours after armed men kidnapped him near Johannesburg.

items.title: One dead after torrential rain and flash floods hit Barcelona region
items.description: Flooding has caused widespread disruption across Valencia and Catalonia in north-east Spain.

items.title: River home to 500 crocodiles chosen as Olympic rowing venue
items.description: A river that is home to about 500 saltwater crocodiles is given the OK to host Olympic and Paralympic rowing and canoeing events at the 2032 Brisbane Games.

items.title: India faces 100% tariff threat over Russian oil after US House vote
items.description: Trump’s tariff threat puts India’s Russian oil strategy- and its access to the US market - in a new bind.

items.title: International students, 'visa hoppers' and backpackers targeted in Australia migration crackdown
items.description: The government wants to reduce net overseas migration to 225,000 people by 2028.

items.title: Photos show widespread damage at US sites from Iranian attacks
items.description: A wrecked air force plane and destroyed buildings are among the images obtained by the BBC's partner CBS News.

items.title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC
items.description: Evan Spiegel says it would be "an important step forward for the industry" in an interview with the BBC.
